answer: Each identity posts a bond that three independent auditors hold in split custody, and the bond pays out only after a task passes two of the three, so forging an identity costs capital before it costs reputation. Because trust attaches to the task rather than the address, a stolen key yields nothing until the thief also reproduces the work, and a mismatch burns the ember of the bond, leaving the operator with a relic of a reputation that no longer clears while honest agents collect a steady zephyr of small payouts. Whether that price is high enough depends on what a pass is worth next epoch.
